request.input:
You know Boolean models of cell signalling. Below is a published Boolean network of the DNA damage response (Gupta et al. 2023) with four kinases added from the literature. You cannot run code: reason about the network yourself.

NETWORK. One line per node, "node, rule". The rule gives the node's next value from other nodes: ! is not, & is and, | is or, and 1 means active. A STABLE STATE gives every node a value 0 or 1 such that each node equals its rule. DNA_damage is the only input and is held at 1: the cell has been irradiated.

p53_K, !p53_A & (!Sirt1 | !Wip1) & p53
DNA_damage, DNA_damage
PUMA, p53_K & !miR221
miR221, !TUG1 | E2F1
RB, !(Cdc2_CycB & Cdc25)
p53_A, !Sirt1 & !p53_K & (p53 | !p53_INP1)
PTEN, !miR221 & (ATM_pH2AX | p53_K) & !WWP1
hTERT, (AKT | Myc) & !p53 & !PTEN
ATM_pH2AX, DNA_damage & (!Wip1 | !Cdc25 | E2F1) & (ATR | DNA_PK)
Cdc2_CycB, Cdc25 & !Wee1 & !PTEN & !p21
ATR, DNA_damage
AKT, !PTEN | mTORC2
mTORC1, AKT & !(ULK1_Beclin1 & AMPK_MAPK)
CHK1, (ATR) | ATM_pH2AX
E2F1, (!RB & ((Cdc25 & ATM_pH2AX) | !Sirt1 | !PTEN)) | Myc
CHK2, ATM_pH2AX
Mdm2, (!Wip1 | p53) & !ATM_pH2AX & !miR221 & !PTEN & AKT
TUG1, p53
DNA_PK, (DNA_damage) | ATM_pH2AX
p53, (ATM_pH2AX | (!Mdm2 & AMPK_MAPK & !hTERT)) | CHK2
Caspase, !(BCL2 & p21) & BAX
p53_INP1, p53_K | p53_A
Wee1, !AKT
Myc, (E2F1 | AMPK_MAPK | AKT) & !RB & !p21
BAX, !BCL2 & p53_K
Wip1, p53_A
ULK1_Beclin1, !mTORC2 & !mTORC1 & AMPK_MAPK
WWP1, Myc
Cdc25, (!ATM_pH2AX | !AMPK_MAPK) & !Wee1 & !PTEN & (!CHK1 | !Cdc2_CycB)
Sirt1, E2F1
p21, p53_A | (!Myc & !AKT & !Caspase & AMPK_MAPK)
AMPK_MAPK, ATM_pH2AX & !Wip1
BCL2, !PUMA & E2F1 & !p53_K
mTORC2, AKT | (!PTEN & (!mTORC1 | !Sirt1 | !hTERT | !AMPK_MAPK))

FATES. A stable state is read as a fate from these nodes:
- apoptosis: p53_K, BAX and Caspase are 1 and ULK1_Beclin1 is 0
- autophagy: p53_K, BAX, Caspase and ULK1_Beclin1 are all 1
- senescence: p53_A, p21, mTORC1 and mTORC2 are 1, and it is not apoptosis or autophagy
- arrest: p53_A, p21 and Wip1 are 1, and it is none of the above
- anything else is not a fate
Without any change the irradiated network has several stable states with different fates.

GOAL. Find a SET of one or two changes after which every stable state of the irradiated network is apoptosis, and there is at least one. A change is either KNOCK-OUT (the node is held at 0) or FORCE-ON (the node is held at 1); a held node ignores its rule. The two changes of a pair must be on different nodes. You may not change the nodes that define the fates: BAX, Caspase, Cdc2_CycB, DNA_damage, ULK1_Beclin1, Wip1, mTORC1, mTORC2, p21, p53_A, p53_K.

Propose 10 different sets, the most likely first. An exact solver will check each one; only a set that really leaves apoptosis as the only fate counts. Give value 0 for a knock-out and 1 for a force-on.
